name: Zhizhu Kuanzhong capsules (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Contains Bupleurum (lung-injury signal in Japanese reports) and bitter orange. Trials in dyspepsia and reflux: no serious adverse reactions; milder events not described. No liver report names it.
text: Studies: a 2019 meta-analysis of 23 randomized trials (2,496 people with functional dyspepsia), mostly of poor methodological quality, of the capsules alone or added to Western medicine reports that no serious adverse reactions were reported. In a randomized trial of 320 people with functional dyspepsia in four groups of 80 (electroacupuncture, the capsules, both, or Western medicines), adverse reactions were monitored and no serious adverse reaction was reported in any group. In a randomized trial of 480 people with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease in four groups (electroacupuncture, the capsules, both, or Western medicines), no serious adverse reactions were found. A 2022 health technology assessment of four Chinese patent medicines for functional dyspepsia (49 of 110 studies on these capsules), of generally low-quality literature, reports no serious adverse reactions for the four medicines, without giving results for each. None of these abstracts gives the number or type of milder events. The 392-person placebo-controlled trial of the capsules in functional dyspepsia, and a 113-person trial in refractory functional dyspepsia comparing the capsules with doxepin (both groups also given omeprazole), do not report adverse events in their abstracts. Herbs: a laboratory study in rats states that the formula contains four botanical drugs: immature bitter orange fruit (Citrus aurantium), Atractylodes macrocephala rhizome, Bupleurum root and hawthorn fruit; it does not say whether the capsules differ. Bupleurum root (Japanese reporting data; the abstract does not name these capsules): in a Japanese adverse drug event report database, reporting signals for drug-induced interstitial lung disease, which the authors call a severe adverse event, were found for 32 of 54 herbal medicines, including Bupleurum root; the abstract gives adjusted reporting odds ratios for Scutellaria root and Pinellia tuber but none for Bupleurum root, and the authors conclude that the lung disease was dose-dependent on the crude drugs; this is a database association, not a study of this formula. PubMed searches found no report of liver injury, kidney injury or heavy-metal contamination naming these capsules. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
